title: introduce-kms-proxy-rotation-controller-and-envelope-migration
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private installs using customer KMS/HSM devices require a safe, upgradeable rotation path that doesn't force full cluster downtime. This PR introduces a lightweight 'kms-proxy-rotation-controller' that coordinates staged TLS/key rotations and provides an envelope-based migration utility for sealed-secrets so clusters can transition to wrapped keys produced by on-prem HSMs. The controller is designed to be rollback-safe: old keys remain valid for verification during a transition window and a derived-transition-token scheme lets services confirm a chain-of-trust without exposing raw material from the HSM.

What this PR includes (high level):
- New Helm chart additions: charts/redwood-private/templates/kms-proxy-controller.yaml, a configurable post-install helm test job, and additional values for HSM/KMIP settings.
- Terraform module changes: modules/kms/main.tf and modules/kms/outputs.tf add IAM roles, KMS binding policies for the rotation controller service account, and a new resource to register 'kms-proxy' endpoints with VPC DNS.
- Migration tooling: scripts/migrate-sealedsecrets-envelope.sh converts existing SealedSecret resources to the new envelope-v2 format that uses HSM-wrapped DEKs (data encryption keys). Tool runs in read-only dry-run mode by default.
- Runtime changes: a small controller binary (packaged into the Helm chart) that performs: 1) staged publish of new public key blob, 2) issuance of transition tokens signed by the old key and wrapped by the HSM for the new key, and 3) healthchecks/metrics exposed for rollout dashboards.
- Docs and runbook: docs/ops/kms_rotation_playbook.md with step-by-step upgrade and rollback instructions and suggested SLO thresholds to stop a rollout.

Design notes: the proxy implements a key-derivation step so that two different key versions can be validated during the overlap window without requiring services to keep both raw keys. This is implemented via a signed 'transition token' that encodes the new key ID wrapped by the HSM and signed by the old key. Services validate signatures with the old public key until the transition window ends, then switch to the new public key. All HSM operations are proxied over KMIP and authenticated using the tenant's existing vault identity (Vault token or KMS credentials are pluggable via Helm values).

Compatibility: backward-compatible with existing sealed-secrets <= v0.18; the migration script supports labels to opt-out per-namespace. Helm chart bump: charts/redwood-private v2.4.0. Terraform module introduces breaking-change-free additions (no removal of existing resources).

Testing: added an e2e helm test (tests/e2e/kms_rotation_test.yaml) that simulates key rotation using a mock KMIP server and validates that SealedSecrets can be decrypted during and after transition. CI also includes a short-lived integration job that runs the migration script in dry-run mode against a snapshot cluster.

Rollout plan (short): staged canary rollout: enable controller in a single cluster, run migration in dry-run, promote migrated sealed secrets in small namespaces, watch metrics for decrypt errors, then expand. Rollback preserves old key and transition tokens until cleanup window expires.

Notes/risks: HSM vendor quirks (KMIP behavior) were addressed via a pluggable adapter layer. Operators must validate HSM-supported key-wrap algorithms; the default adapter falls back to a software-wrapped DEK for vendors without KMIP support.

Checklist:
- [x] Helm templates and values updated
- [x] Terraform additions and docs
- [x] Migration script with dry-run
- [x] E2E helm test added
- [x] Ops runbook drafted

References: Linear tickets ENG-8421 (rotation controller), ENG-8473 (sealed-secrets envelope migration), SUP-2104 for customer repro steps attached to customer case.

release_notes: Add a new kms-proxy rotation controller to coordinate safe key rotations for HSM-backed KMS; includes a migration utility for sealed-secrets to envelope-v2 format, Helm chart updates (redwood-private v2.4.0), and Terraform module additions to register proxy endpoints and IAM bindings. Operators must follow the ops playbook for staged rollout. Backwards compatible by default.
